pages.text: A creature is not its flesh. Flesh is only where its $(l)attributes$() happen to be kept. Draw them out and the flesh does strange things without them.$(br2)I count five, so far.

$(l)Density$(): weight, belonging to the ground.$(br)$(l)Speed$(): how quickly it moves and acts.$(br)$(l)Size$(): how much of the world it fills.$(br)$(l)Awareness$(): the mind, the noticing.$(br)$(l)Time$(): its age, and everything it has left.

Every kind of creature carries its own measure of each, which I record in $(l)drams$().$(br2)What is taken $(o)does not grow back$(). A cow I have drained stays drained. Calves, however, are born whole.
pages.title: Drams
